#image("/imgs/ap-calc-bc-2003-frq-02-diagram-01.jpg", width: 65%)

A particle starts at point $A$ on the positive $x$-axis at time $t = 0$ and travels along the curve from $A$ to $B$ to $C$ to $D$, as shown above. The coordinates of the particle's position $(x(t)\, y(t))$ are differentiable functions of $t$, where $x'(t)= frac(d x,d t)= - 9 cos lr((frac(pi t,6))) sin lr((frac(pi sqrt(t + 1),2)))$ and $y'(t)= frac(d y,d t)$ is not explicitly given. At time $t = 9$, the particle reaches its final position at point $D$ on the positive $x$-axis.

(a) At point $C$, is $frac(d y,d t)$ positive? At point $C$, is $frac(d x,d t)$ positive? Give a reason for each answer.

(b) The slope of the curve is undefined at point $B$. At what time $t$ is the particle at point $B$ ?

(c) The line tangent to the curve at the point $(x(8)\, y(8))$ has equation $y = frac(5,9) x - 2$. Find the velocity vector and the speed of the particle at this point.

(d) How far apart are points $A$ and $D$, the initial and final positions, respectively, of the particle?
